## Booking

Ryokan Kamosui, ten minutes from Demachiyanagi station. 6 nights, 8 to 14 April 2024. ¥38,500 per night for two
including breakfast; kaiseki dinner only on the first night (+¥9,000 each, worth it once, not twice). Confirmation
KMS-24-0408-19, deposit of ¥20,000 paid back in February. The owner, Mrs. Okuhara, speaks basically zero English,
which turned every check-in chat into homework for [[Japanese kanji study]].

## Getting there from Osaka

Hankyu line from Umeda, ¥410, 44 minutes. Nobody needs the shinkansen for that hop, I don't care what the blogs say.
Topped up the ICOCA with ¥3,000 at Umeda. The four eating-my-way-through-Osaka days just before are in
[[大阪の食べ歩き]].

## Fushimi Inari at dawn

Alarm at 5:20. On the gates by 6:10 and it was almost empty, just a jogger and a cat. Reached the Yotsutsuji
viewpoint at 6:55. Coming down at 8:30 it was already a wall of selfie sticks. Bought a little fox-face ema for ¥800
and drew a terrible fox on it.

## Temples I actually liked

- Hōnen-in: moss-covered gate, free, nobody there at 9am
- Kōtō-in (inside Daitoku-ji): ¥500, the maple corridor, sat there for 40 minutes
- Kinkaku-ji: gorgeous and packed, 15 minutes max
- Ginkaku-ji: the sand cone is weird and lovely

The Philosopher's Path was still pink on 9 April, petals floating in the canal. Kenji told me a lot of these temples
lost land in the [[Meiji restoration]], which explains the oddly small grounds of some of them.

## Uji and matcha

Day trip on 11 April, JR Nara line, ¥240. Tasted three grades at Kōsen-dō, a tiny tea shop by the river, ¥1,650 for
the set. Bought a 40 g tin of their "Shiun" grade for ¥2,800. Whisked it badly at the ryokan. For the quiet,
meditative side of tea there's [[禅と茶道]].

## Food

- Nishiki market: tamagoyaki on a stick ¥300, soy milk doughnuts ¥400 for 10
- Yudofu set near Nanzen-ji, ¥3,300: bland, beautiful, would not repeat
- Best meal of the trip: okonomiyaki counter "Hirata" in Demachi, ¥1,100, eight seats, grandma at the griddle

## Getting around

The old bus day pass was discontinued, so subway plus ICOCA. Rented bikes from Kamogawa Cycle at ¥1,000 a day and
that was the real move: the city is flat and the river path is perfect at golden hour.

## UX nerd corner

Kyoto bus stop displays show the next three buses as dots creeping along a line. Instantly readable without a single
word. Took about 40 photos of signage for my inspo folder; the station wayfinding colours are their own masterclass.

## Spend

Roughly ¥184,000 for the six days on top of the ryokan. Most of it was food and tea, zero regrets.
